name: Hashrate re-arm in a risk-on macro regime — slow on-chain capital aligned with macro tailwind
rationale: Crypto trends backed by miner commitment are far more likely to extend when the macro backdrop is also risk-on rather than fighting a tightening tape. The thesis stacks two orthogonal slow signals: btc_hashrate crosses UP (on-chain slow capital — miners — re-arms) WHILE the composite macro_regime is above a fitted floor (the macro backdrop is risk-supportive) AND momentum is positive. The combination requires BOTH the network-internal conviction signal and the external liquidity/risk backdrop to agree before going long spot. macro_regime is a BOUNDED composite gated by gt on its level; btc_hashrate is drifting and read ONLY via cross_up/cross_down. Exit when macro turns (macro_regime lt exit) or miners capitulate. Disconfirmer (core falsifier): the edge must come from miner re-commitment adding orthogonal info to the macro gate. If replacing the btc_hashrate cross_up arm with an always-true pass (keeping macro_regime>floor + ret_Nd>0) matches or beats deflated Sharpe, hashrate is redundant and this collapses to a macro-armed momentum trade. Low-confidence until OOS; the Gate decides.
catalyst: btc_hashrate crosses up while macro_regime is risk-on and momentum is positive
